Codex PASS lacked valid task or source evidence for every premise. PASS for the exact PARTIAL mathematical review. The retained conclusions in n1–n3 and the mathematical gap analysis in n4 are established under the expressly granted full P13.1 body. This verdict does not establish the original P13.2 image characterization or existence theorem. Documentary and operational observations were excluded from the review.

The grant is used within its stated scope: actual cone classes, calibrated rational quotients, genuine positive same-field products, integration by parts and Hodge negativity, weighted decreasing-net continuity, intrinsic roots, and outer-energy differentiation. No envelope attainment, strong I-completeness, inverse MA existence, or cross-Reeb mixed calculus is added. The task-grant passage has index −1 because granted background is excluded from the external-premises list.

Normalization checks pass. The rational product reference gives the trivial-valuation Dirac probability; the granted radial calibration and bounded irrational-reference passage preserve that probability. Hence normalized potentials satisfy sup_K u=u(v_triv)=0 and J(u)=−E(u). The factors V_eta=s^(−n)d^(1−n)(L_d^p), (omega_eta^p)=sV_eta, E_eta=E_Ld/(sd), and E=(n+1)S/n remain unchanged. The polynomial construction keeps V^(−1) and the fixed radial factor dd^c rho^+ throughout.

For n1, the decreasing-integral argument works for nets on a nonmetrizable compact Hausdorff carrier. Radon regularity supplies continuous majorants; compactness and directedness make each continuous majorant, enlarged by epsilon, eventually dominate the decreasing net. This proves the asserted integral limit, including −infinity. Together with decreasing energy continuity, it establishes integrability of every actual E1 potential when L(mu) is finite and equality of the FS, CPSH, and E1 dual suprema.

The converse is also valid. If integration were unbounded on normalized J≤1, the weighted convex partial sums would decrease to a nontrivial actual PSH potential with energy at least −1 and infinite negative target integral. Thus the limit is E1 and contradicts the integrability hypothesis. The segment expansion has b_0=0 and gives J(tu)≤2^n t²J(u). Scaling then yields the stated bound L(mu)≤B+2^(n−2)B². The normalized root bounds and onto-E1 property consequently transport the finite-energy target class on the same K, without transporting a strong topology.

The concave tangent inequality has the correct sign. Its raw decreasing approximation gives L(MA(u))=E(u)−∫u dMA(u), finite for genuine E1 outputs. Applying both signs of outer differentiation to the target deficit yields the continuous-test error d_u/s+C_f s. Density and probability mass one then give genuine weak convergence for maximizing FS outputs. The argument also applies to any maximizing net by choosing s first and then making the deficit small; no countable enumeration of the carrier or field is needed.

The midpoint calculation passes. The Green kernel is one half of min(t,1−t); retaining [1/4,3/4] gives exactly the valid lower constant a_p=p/4^(p+1). Therefore I(u,v)≤(d_u+d_v)/(2a_p), and J(u)≤I(u,0)≤(d_u+L)/(2a_p). Weighted decreasing continuity passes these formulas to E1. Maximizing potentials are I-Cauchy modulo constants, and the stated Hodge estimate proves MA continuity at an actual E1 I-limit. Its existence remains an explicit antecedent.

For n2, the fixed-ray linear construction is legitimate. A relation among restrictions extends to the same relation among zero-slope functions, so the signed products are independent of presentations. Any direction in the span can be expressed as a positive multiple of a difference of two actual CPSH potentials by padding with the reference. In the cone P, a slot with s>0 has curvature s dd^c u for an actual same-field u; a boundary constant slot has zero curvature. Thus Hodge negativity gives the required quadratic positivity for every kernel direction and every positive slot.

Expanding the genuine energy gives H(1,u)=E(u), since binom(p,l)/(l+1)=binom(p+1,l+1)/(p+1). Integration by parts gives ∂_dH[f]=V^(−1)∫f Omega^p dd^c rho^+. Two derivatives produce coefficient −p, whereas polarization produces (p+1)p, confirming the factor −1/(p+1) in (25). The deficit expansion consequently gives I/(p+1)≤delta≤pI/(p+1), delta+delta_reverse=I, and delta(u,0)=J(u). These calculations establish the exact Appendix A hypotheses without linearizing nonlinear roots.

I opened and checked [Appendix A of 2307.01697v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.01697v1), including its pertinent proof bodies. The square-root recurrence and quasi-triangle absorption are valid, with dimension-dependent constants retained. Its Hölder application yields (33) with alpha=2^(−p). For p=1 the argument reduces to quadratic Cauchy–Schwarz, and the factor with exponent zero is one.

The target-estimate limit order is correct. For each fixed continuous approximant of phi, first send the maximizing measures to mu. Then send the raw decreasing potential net to phi, using target integrability for mu and weighted continuity for the fixed MA(psi). Subtracting the convergent trivial-valuation constants does not require the normalized approximants to decrease. With J(w_k)≤B0 and I(phi,0)≤(p+1)J(phi), this proves the exact signed estimate (2). Equations (35)–(37) follow: bounded-J uniform signed convergence, convergence of genuine output dual energies, and Cauchyness of maximizing-sequence target integrals and normalized energies. They establish no absolute L1 continuity for arbitrary weak potential nets and no actual potential limit.

The n3 strict-support argument includes infinite coordinates correctly. Positive supported coefficients with sum less than one give strict convexity on the finite face and positive recession cost in every nonzero finite-coordinate direction. Bounded difference sublevels confine those coordinates and bound the remaining coordinates below, proving compactness and the positive gap outside any contact neighborhood. Empty finite-coordinate sets are included.

The multinomial maxima have the claimed uniform error on the extended product. Rational rounding and the separated epsilon levels make the approximants decrease. Terms beta_i=1, beta_0=m−1 retain the original generators themselves. In the pole-sensitive construction, F_ij≤D_iH and the epsilon differences prove monotonicity; the rational upper coefficients prove domination even when logarithms are negative. A positive lower multiple of H permits original-generator branches to be appended without changing the function. At a supported logarithmic pole the limit is −infinity pointwise; no uniform pole approximation is asserted. These presentations meet the actual definition in [2609.27610v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.27610v1).

The normal localization implication retains its full antecedent (42). Divisor rays give orders of the actual rational functions, not denominator exponents. For q/r>c/a, every height-one order of h^r f^q is nonnegative, so the granted normal-domain intersection property puts this element in the original A. The hull inequality gives the error 2a(q/r)M; taking decreasing rational ratios yields exactly 2cM. The zero cases avoid subtracting infinities. This does not establish controlled approximation of a weak localized input.

The retraction lemma is valid without openness: inverse images of carrier neighborhoods supply one usc inequality, and restriction of ambient neighborhoods supplies the other. Rational carrier-envelope membership follows under the explicitly retained projective EP antecedent. On K×R, uniform orbit slopes and the action homeomorphisms give both raw-root identities, including roots equal to −infinity. This transports membership after a base exists; it proves no unconditional normal EP or completeness result.

The n4 gap analysis passes. The lower-growth counterexample is locally psh by decreasing rational secants, satisfies g≤g²+1/4, and cannot have a global decreasing AFS majorant because its Gauss-ray growth is quadratic. The cited envelope proof depends on the weak/global chain it leaves unresolved. Continuous integer traces need only be locally constant on disconnected opens; the two-disk square-map construction gives traces two and one, and gamma=1 needs separate treatment. These rejected source bridges are not premises of the retained theorem. The synthetic measure-completeness theorem likewise supplies no actual E1 realization here.

For n=1, the granted effective normal grading gives R=k[z], K={v_triv}, E(c)=c, and the sole probability; realization is immediate modulo constants. The p≥1 estimates are not applied with a_0 or a negative target exponent.

Harmless precisions: choose positive rational lower coefficients q_ij, or discard a finite initial tail; interpret uniform upper bounds for equivariant families on K; retain implicit dimension constants in the Appendix A proof; and interpret zero exponents as one. No substantive repair is needed.
